score_reasons.quality: The poster is roughly two-thirds pure black; the only pictorial content is a small, extremely underexposed fragment at top where stone walls and vague shapes are barely discernible, so material, edge and detail quality cannot hold up — a picture-level hard defect. The text block itself is cleanly typeset.
score_reasons.aesthetics: Composition collapses into a black void with floating white text; the murky top fragment neither reads as a scene nor creates mood. Title/subtitle/date stacking is orderly, but there is almost no visual interest, light or atmosphere to evaluate positively.
score_reasons.alignment: Title, subtitle and a short date line are present and the no-micro-print constraint is respected, but the core premise — a WeChat Moments interface of the Xuanwu Gate Incident — is entirely absent (no UI, feed, avatars, likes), and the background scene is too dark to depict any recognizable event content. The date line reads as nonsense ('20周年 6/12').
score_reasons.real_world_fidelity: Almost nothing is verifiable due to the darkness; the vague ruins are generic, and the invented '20周年 6/12' line has no relation to the 626 CE historical event, weakening cultural fidelity. No visible anachronisms, but also no substantive period content.
score_reasons.creative_generation: Minimal creative execution: a near-black canvas with overlaid text and an illegible fragment; the mashup concept was not attempted, and there is no imaginative world-building or layered storytelling to credit.
